### 2026-11-03: Today I thought of my main idea and imported the parts I want to use into KiCad. Firstly I followed the flight controller guide, and started with the main python script and began listing parts from LC

**3h**

Today I thought of my main idea and imported the parts I want to use into KiCad. Firstly I followed the flight controller guide, and started with the main python script and began listing parts from LCSC, however, the script had some problems.

Importing the main script:

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 221959](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/5ed1ca1b1943a753faffcd603a65b7c4b80a812bf2fa40d5bf4c39c89f379cf8.png)

The errors were a bit painful to solve. The terminal showing the actual error popped up for a singular nanosecond, and then disappeared, leaving me a small window to screenshot the error and send it to Cursor. Apparently it wouldn't read the file, even if it was placed right next to it.

Error:

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 223649](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/9f75adac4b8149142d687bcde7ec730d170fbf115efc157bbd98cb254b21044d.png)

After much trial and tribulation, I got past the errors and actually started importing the parts as Ki-Cad usable libraries. I looked up footprints for these circuits/components:
USB-C
MicroSD
TPS63070
LMR51430
BQ25883
STM32F722RETx
ICM-45686
BMP580
Optional LED

Looking for components:

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 225258](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/0a0acac590cdac8bb15a65c13eb6a5a0c495193705d938d3c96e673d60176c75.png)

From here, I don't actually know if I'm going to end up with something that flies, but what I get from following this guide is what I get. For now, I'm going to import the parts into KiCad and connect the components, make the PCB (hello painful routing!) and then finalize the code for the sensors. Whatever time I have left will be a horrible attempt to bring it into the real world.

### 2026-11-04: I finished the USB-C and the battery charger today. This project alone was a lot more than I was expecting. I don't think I'll be able to  be ambitious or go bigger with this project, having a flight

**3h**

I finished the USB-C and the battery charger today. This project alone was a lot more than I was expecting. I don't think I'll be able to  be ambitious or go bigger with this project, having a flight controller alone is a great achievement. Anyhow, I followed the guide, and wired the USB-C with the proper resistors, wirings to ground, and finally, the pins connected to each other that I needed.

USB-C:

![Screenshot 2026-11-03 222423](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/43cc30c05cddfb325294be5905f9ad67bd4762ab730773f5aa42d50378368071.png)

Next was the big kahuna, aside from the rest of the chips (once again, I fear the day I have to make the PCB traces), the BQ25883RGER, or in English, the battery charging circuit. I wired that up, taking a long time, setting each of the resistor, capacitor, and inductor voltages. It took a loooong time. It wasn't hard, just tedious. Trying to get all the components in the right place, flipping between the guide and sketch, and not knowing the symbol for an inductor took quite the time. After a long, arduous process, the battery charging circuit was wired.

Battery Charging circuit:

![Screenshot 2026-11-03 220128](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/2ec45fec221df61a7b621fc98f65ed3f5f94e2009924d1c91d611e153046324e.png)

Onto the future, I intend to finish this flight controller as a test of my KiCad skills, and as a testament to my hard work and effort. Perhaps in the future, I might add some motors and try to make something that flies, but for now, this is what I'm going to do.

Progress so far:

![Screenshot 2026-11-03 220151](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/9ad69ef5f909f2f50f3919d9c0eb4e5960d6304247a292fc11947ae35b645577.png)

### 2026-11-05: Day 3 Week 5

**5h**

Day 3 Week 5

Today, I finished most of the components and began work on the main microcontroller. First, I have to address the elephant in the room. If you've seen my previous journals, you'd know that they're a lot more wordy and descriptive. Over here, it's not too wordy at all. That's because I'm following the tutorial, and there isn't really much to say without repeating what the tutorial says, or just saying "I followed the schematic according to the tutorial.", or something stupid like that.

Anyway, I began connecting up the TPS63070RNMR, or the regulators in plain English. It genuinely feels nerve wracking, as the components I imported aren't the same as the one on the guide pictures, but using my electronics knowledge (and my ability to read pin names), I'm able to connect them accordingly.

Routing the regulators:

![Screenshot 2026-11-04 222140](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/797f9e4b7133e18a07ab193b5b51523a144388d3f1ff888f411f75da064075a7.png)

Next, I did the LMR51430, another regulator. This one was a bit smaller but much of the same. Eventually I'll have to add these things to the PCB, and I guess I'll try to do the same exact thing that the guide does, I can't do any unique designs for this project without SUBSTANSIAL extra pain.

Routed LMR51430:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/9796b621fdb813a415b7b3ce8eee83955629d92a4c21e71d60df27856697060b.png)

Now that I was done with the power components, I began working  on the sensors and MicroSD. Next up was the BMP580 (another banger name), which is a sensor that measures barometric pressure and altimeter. This one was going to be important to the aircraft. I don't know too much about aircraft, but I think that knowing how high you are is kind of important. I finished up that component and moved onto the next.

Routed BMP580:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/d5fd631c4b28653daa328a847c41618f3087f52997bad7bdc647cfaa242ed5ae.png)

Next was the ICM-45686, another sensor with an ultra-low-noise 6-axis MEMS (Micro-Electro-Mechanical System) motion tracking sensor, with a 3-axis gyroscope, and a 3-axis accelerometer. This one will measure how fast the aircraft is going, and how the aircraft is oriented, so for example, if we want to add a stabilizing system later, we can detect if the aircraft is tipping over one side, and then run the propellors accordingly to make it hover again.

Routed ICM-45686:

![Screenshot 2026-11-04 224155](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/84e0fc6568e8573489eb9cf787495ac1aa0dc8204227690b08c46325e6a28da6.png)

Finally, the MicroSD was the final component, containing the data and program for the flight controller to run. I know that software is obviously important, otherwise we just have a hunk of metal. Anywho, I did the MicroSD, which has a slightly different .sch than the one on the guide. Oh well.

Routed MicroSD:

![Screenshot 2026-11-04 225822](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/720eb85c462cc7b1952511563ced6fbec938cae90a6f98c76d529be066b9e202.png)

After all that, I still have to route the big kahuna, the STM32F722RET6, or the main microcontroller for this project, and then the PCB, which the traces will be a nightmare, and the rest of this project. From here, I downloaded the software for this microcontroller, and left it at that. Once again, I might expand on this project after Half-Life, to make it into something that flies, but for now I'll end up with the board for it.

My progress at the end:

![Screenshot 2026-11-04 225822](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/720eb85c462cc7b1952511563ced6fbec938cae90a6f98c76d529be066b9e202.png)

### 2026-11-07: Week 5, day 5 - Downfall (part 2)

**3h**

Week 5, day 5 - Downfall (part 2)

Today, I finished the schematics, the footprints, and created the PCB. First, I started with finishing up the STM32, the main brains of the project. It didn't take long, as all the other components were done. The schematic was now finished, just missing the footprints, and/or some minor tweaks I might need to make.

Finished schematics:

![Screenshot 2026-11-06 224128](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/b0621f9fef17fc6282aaeb049c79fd1b949aa78a95b215b930dfafc7d512f292.png)

Next was the footprints for the PCB. I followed the guide, but there were still some parts and footprints I needed to use, so I asked AI. It gave me which footprints to use for specific capacitors and resistors, and each footprint for the core components.

Me working on the footprints:

![Screenshot 2026-11-06 234613](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/e2c178353b75b5b2388d727b3d78cf5b45a2cc6b2f22420e0a81675929936e1e.png)

Next, I imported the schematic into the PCB editor, and immediately i noticed a few problems with how KiCad auto-assigns footprints. I'm not an electronics expert (yet), but I don't think a capacitor has 60+ pins, and it's own dedicated chip. It was back to looking through the schematic, seeing what was wrong, fixing it, going back, and doing the same. After this, I had a somewhat workable footprint, and a base for building the PCB, although I might need to improve it later. I could go on further, but as of typing this, it's 12 in the morning and I need some sleep, so I'll do the PCB tomorrow...

PCB:

![Screenshot 2026-11-06 235718](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/dfa8637eea08d00f96c8e63376a0e104d287ddc925616f3c296e9df316ef6c73.png)

### 2026-11-08: Week 5 - Day 6 - When you hit rock bottom...

**4h**

Week 5 - Day 6 - When you hit rock bottom...

This journal entry is a short one, because I am COMPLETELY burnt out and demoralized. It's 1:45 in the morning, and I lost lots of progress, with only 1 day remaining to do EVERYTHING. I started on the PCB, laying out components to get a rough idea of which one needs what capacitors, resistors, looking though the schematics and organizing until I had this.

![Screenshot 2026-11-07 212459](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/a529ccebeb5ae65e9c7e6ad64532cac5583d3b3b22b9f910704235203406feb1.png)

I then created a 100x100 mm PCB, following the advice from last week so that It wouldn't be too expensive, and then put the grouped components onto it, along with strategically planning out the routes so that I would have an easier time routing.

![Screenshot 2026-11-07 221623](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/92eac0b836f988488424bbd5d14c9bf98e44797b9142b5bca3d8e198c40f2b4f.png)

Next came the actual routing. I routed the USB port, part of the STM microcontroller, and another IC that I can't remember. It was around this time that I saved and took a small break. This is important for later. After a bit of doomscrolling, it was back to the grind and I had finished routing the entire board 10 minutes prior. I then, and pardon my French here, made a "very little" fucky-wucky. I closed the PCB editor, the popup came up asking if I wanted to save, and I clicked "Don't Save". I remember that moment, my brain realizing I had made a mistake, but my hand was already committed to the action, and I had lost several hours of progress.

Me routing some of the components:
![Screenshot 2026-11-07 232029](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/da6bae10e434aa5cd35f62e0c1d3ea0601c50eb9089d6a1f91bdd894a815430a.png)

So here I am, back at SQUARE ONE, leaving the BOM, GitHub, and god forbid, the entire damn routing job I treaded through with blood, sweat, and tears. Here is what I have left.

![Screenshot 2026-11-08 014306](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5Di8qxPvTjh464E0buJSS1rL8xZfVQiB/b2c7b6e6d93d30907b61cad3e1d78b9937457c8a8d4981b95f2d8071dc7b8712.png)
